bug_semantics: In filebrowser v2, an authenticated user confined to an otherwise-authorized scope but configured with Perm.Download=false can send GET /api/resources/<same-scope-file>?checksum=md5|sha1|sha256|sha512. resourceGetHandler invokes FileInfo.Checksum, which reads the file, and renderJSON returns the digest without checking Download. This bypasses only the Download permission, not scope/path authorization: it exposes a content-hash oracle usable for known-content confirmation, change detection, or offline guessing of low-entropy content, and forces a full-file read. The vulnerable v2 implementation is present from v2.0.0-rc.1 (and stable v2.0.0) through v2.63.18; v2.63.19 closes it.
flaw_origin: The canonical master landing 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 ('feat: v2 (#599)') is a one-parent aggregate of the v2 pull-request history, not the smallest BIC. Decomposing the still-public refs/pull/575/head history identifies member 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266 ('feat: many updates (see PR)') as the first writer: in one patch it creates types/user.go with Permissions.Download and creates http/resource.go with the /api/resources checksum branch, which calls file.Checksum and returns JSON without consulting that new permission. Its direct parent c01ebf33efed835680373668e54d9ddafc90a6b1 has neither the v2 /api/resources handler nor any Download permission, so the bypass is semantically absent. Later commit 1e03feadb550e4414b5589a6a8df57f538efba15 fixed plaintext and X-Encoding reads for CVE-2026-35606 but left this pre-existing checksum branch ungated, making it the residual incomplete-remediation path rather than its first writer.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266` identifies both author and committer as Henrique Dias <hacdias@gmail.com>; the message contains human `Signed-off-by: Henrique Dias <hacdias@gmail.com>` lines and no AI Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI attribution trailer.
evidence: Reproduction from the validated clone plus a temporary object store for public PR refs: (1) `git log -L 69,79:http/resource.go 6c69b5cd895e15b29e563200a9a6dfc27b06525e^` and `git log -S 'if checksum := r.URL.Query().Get("checksum"); checksum != "" {' -- http/resource.go` trace the canonical-history hunk to aggregate 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471. `git ls-remote https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser.git refs/pull/575/head` returns a23f868abb77e53a5bca92022464dab2da7b756c; fetching that ref and running the same -S search plus `git log -L 83,96:http/resource.go 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266` returns member 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266 with parent c01ebf33efed835680373668e54d9ddafc90a6b1. `git show 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266 -- http/resource.go types/user.go` shows both `Download bool` and the unchecked checksum call. `git ls-tree c01ebf33efed835680373668e54d9ddafc90a6b1 -- http/resource.go` is empty and `git grep -n Download c01ebf33efed835680373668e54d9ddafc90a6b1 -- '*.go'` has no match; the parent has an old checksum route but no Download permission to bypass. `git cat-file -p 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266` reproduces the human identities and marker absence. (2) `git show 1e03feadb550e4414b5589a6a8df57f538efba15 -- http/resource.go` shows the CVE-2026-35606 patch changed `Content: true` to `Content: d.user.Perm.Download` and guarded only X-Encoding, leaving checksum untouched. (3) `git show 6c69b5cd895e15b29e563200a9a6dfc27b06525e -- http/resource.go` shows the direct closing fix adding `if !d.user.Perm.Download { return http.StatusAccepted, nil }` immediately before FileInfo.Checksum; its parent is 4b8a8d72ce554dde378b5091da74aa930ea18327 and still lacks the guard. The bundle's b7dc392838f11d188f0bc0f2a1a99fad3f7dca03 reference is not a fix (`git show` changes only the PID/UID typo in www/docs/installation.md); repository CHANGELOG.md names 6c69b5cd895e15b29e563200a9a6dfc27b06525e for the checksum permission fix. (4) `git merge-base --is-ancestor 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 v1.11.0` fails while the checks against v2.0.0-rc.1 and v2.0.0 succeed. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6c69b5cd895e15b29e563200a9a6dfc27b06525e v2.63.18` fails and the v2.63.19 check succeeds; `git tag --contains 6c69b5cd895e15b29e563200a9a6dfc27b06525e --sort=version:refname` starts at v2.63.19. The first-party advisory states affected <=2.63.18 and patched 2.63.19.
reasoning: The security invariant was introduced together with the v2 Download permission: every operation that derives file content for a user with Download=false must stop before reading or returning that derived content. PR member 42227d9edd7ce613e8b6c0ad62c8cad16cf77266 created both sides but omitted the invariant in the checksum branch; its parent cannot exhibit this permission bypass. Canonical commit 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 merely aggregates the public v2 history, and later refactors did not originate the hunk. Commit 1e03feadb550e4414b5589a6a8df57f538efba15 was an incomplete remediation because it protected plaintext/X-Encoding paths only; 6c69b5cd895e15b29e563200a9a6dfc27b06525e directly guards checksum and is included first in v2.63.19. The only admissible AI evidence is the decomposed BIC commit object, whose human author/committer and message contain no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of AI assistance disclosed in the much later advisory investigation.
